result:
Round 257 is planned and the decision is **CONTINUE**. It is a small fix-up that finishes SABA-B-9 stage 1.

**What happened in round 256.** C failed the round on one Medium bug, C-R256-01. Play's name is now always "Play", so while music plays a screen reader can no longer tell that it is playing. Only the brass colour shows it. My round-256 task caused this: it removed the old "Pause" label and named no replacement. A's code was fine. The other 16 rows passed in a real browser, and the gate published nothing. So SABA-B-9 stage 1 is marked **ბაგია** (bug), not done.

**My ruling (D-29z492).**
- **Fix:** Play and Stop both get a hidden accessible description, "Playing" or "Stopped" (`aria-describedby` pointing to a hidden span). It adds no visible text, the label stays "Play", and only the transport component changes.
- **Rejected:** `aria-pressed`. It tells a screen reader that a second press releases the button, but a second Play press does nothing.
- **Rejected:** a spoken status message. It would need two files that are frozen this round, and it would compete with the existing status line.
- **Reference:** I could not find how Ableton Live 12 exposes the Play state to screen readers, so the task says "no reference found".
- **Listed deviations:**
  - starting and stopping playback are still not announced aloud;
  - the button's description no longer reads "Play (Space)";
  - `aria-pressed` was rejected.

  The key itself stays in the tooltip and the `?` sheet.

**Round 257 for A** (7 files; every other file is frozen by hash, including the auth and purchase files):
- the transport component and two new strings;
- the strings test, which was the only test that broke when I tried the change on a copy;
- new tests TC10 and TC11, each with a mutant that must turn red;
- C-R256-02 (Low) fixed now: three render-budget tests regain their "still playing" check;
- a stale test title (GS14);
- implementation doc 193.

**Checked before dispatch, on a copy of the working tree:**
- typecheck and lint are clean;
- 170 test files / 2,513 tests, with the single expected failure in the strings test;
- Chromium at both viewports shows "Stopped" / "Playing" on Play and Stop, and the toolbar height is unchanged;
- the jsdom side works too. The repo has no `toHaveAccessibleDescription` matcher, so TC10 uses Testing Library's `description` filter.

**What C checks:** a new screen-reader row (C-A11Y-257), plus short re-runs of the on-state, focus, keyboard, layout, screen-budget, export-hash and auth rows. The other round-256 rows carry over because those files are provably unchanged.

**Also recorded:**
- **Questions for Saba:** two new parts on SABA-Q-9-TRANSPORT. Should Space on a focused Play/Stop button act like a click? Should starting and stopping playback be announced aloud? Neither blocks anything.
- **Lessons:** two clauses added to existing lessons; the file stays at 58 lines.
- **Architecture:** A's `play()`/`stop()` note is filed as a signal, not a task. It goes to root as an addendum (`b-round-256-checkpoint-addendum.md`) to the pending, non-blocking transport checkpoint.
- **Regression round:** not due yet. The last one was 2026-10-27, and a regression round needs a published commit. It comes right after round 257 publishes if the date is 2026-10-30 or later. Then SABA-B-9 stage 2 (master volume bottom-right) and SABA-B-11c.

I did not change any store files; the working tree still has the same 14 round-256 entries. The advisor was available and I used it twice: before the ruling and at the final check. Its final-check fixes are applied.

Files are in `tmp/studio-real-loop/`:
- `current-task.md`
- `tasks/round-256.md` (archived copy)
- `b-round-256.md`
- `b-next.json`
- `backlog.json`
- `feature-status.md`
- `lessons.md`

Sources:
- [Live 12 manual – Accessibility and Keyboard Navigation](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/accessibility-and-keyboard-navigation/)
